why: An old price and a current price sit side by side, and the old one is written first. What a competitor charges today is the current price; the struck-through figure is marketing. Getting this backwards inflates a competitor's price in our report, which is the direction of error most likely to flatter whoever is reading.

Harvest Plan

Was $89 per month. Now $59 per month.

We lowered the price in March after moving off a per-seat license for our mapping provider, and we passed the saving on rather than keeping it. The plan has not changed: multi-site inventory, same-day route changes, and a dedicated account manager are all still included.

Existing customers were moved to the new price automatically and did not need to ask.
